### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `73fd4081b156ee6724f8fa0ac0678601124dc2e0` — the merge of head `61449d236a51cac089b5d331cf301f852f8896dc` into base `40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 73fd4081b156ee6724f8fa0ac0678601124dc2e0 && git checkout 73fd4081b156ee6724f8fa0ac0678601124dc2e0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388 61449d236a51cac089b5d331cf301f852f8896dc && git checkout -B drift-repro 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388 && git merge --no-ff 61449d236a51cac089b5d331cf301f852f8896dc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2bc6c13c6132c07d2952e554727282b0783c52eb`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #15204 body and all 125 comments (the claim amendment 6111348289, the stage-8 seat answer 6110777865 and the dev report 6112530240 among them); objectui#7611 comment 6097763840 (Q1 → A); PR #22881 body, file list and net diff against `main` at this head; ADR-0126 §7.1/§9 and ADR-0131 D3/D4/D6 on `main`; the flow precedent `POST /automation/:name/clone` (`domains/automation.ts`) and the sibling door `domains/catalog-activation.ts` on `main`; the check-runs on this head, re-read at 2026-10-11T19:13Z.

**Gate verdicts on this head (19:13Z):** 29 `success`, including all three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards and their aggregate, `Test Core` 1/2/4/5/6, `Temporal Conformance`, `Check Changeset`, all five type-check lanes, `Spec property liveness` and the three claim guards. **1 `failure`: `Build Docs`** (the step "Build Docs (the command production runs)", `apps/docs` `pnpm run build`, exit 1; its job log sits on a host this seat's proxy refuses, so the cause is read from the diff below). **Still pending at render: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core (3/6)`.** 2 roster skips (Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The route and its mount — right.** `POST /security/permission-sets/:name/clone` is an arm of the dispatcher's `/security` domain, placed after the domain's anonymous floor and the activation arm and before the `suggested-bindings` service probe (`security.ts`), and mounted on the wire by `registerSecurityActivationRoutes` for every base the activation door gets. On `main` nothing in `packages/rest` mounts under `/security/permission-sets` (the discard-overlay row is a RETIRED comment at `rest-route-ledger.ts:421`), so nothing collides. The three green Dogfood shards are the on-the-wire proof; the HTTP pin is in shard scope.
2. **The body accept set — right, one message wrong.** Closed `{ name, label }`, both non-empty strings, `name` judged by `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` — the same rule `PermissionSetSchema.name` declares (`spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts:817`), so the door's pre-check refuses nothing the save would accept and accepts nothing the save would refuse. Unknown keys answer `unknown_field`, a non-object body `invalid_type`, a missing key `required`. **Wrong, text only:** the 400 message says a name may start "with a letter or underscore"; the schema is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` with a minimum of 2, so a leading underscore is refused by the very rule the message explains.
3. **The match predicate — right.** `parts[0] === 'permission-sets' && parts[2] === 'clone'` with no depth bound, and the handler refuses any depth other than 3 with 400 (pinned). That is the flow precedent's "a gate narrower than its route is a bypass" shape.
4. **Authority — right as ruled; one consequence named in ③.** `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict({ operation: 'save' })` is asked before the path, the body and every read: `isSystem` admits, `manage_metadata` admits, anything else (an absent or non-array `systemPermissions` included) is refused 403 (`metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts:85–91`). It is the verdict `domains/meta.ts:879` asks for a save, so the door's authority is the `/meta` door's, which is what #22621 → A fixes. It is not the ADR-0126 §5 activation gate, and the flow precedent says why in its own docblock (`isFlowActivationWrite`: "clone is deliberately NOT here … a clone creates an ordinary new artifact under a new name and takes nothing away from any tenant"). The anonymous 401 is the domain floor's, ahead of the arm.
5. **The source read — right.** `securityCatalogReaderOf(ql).resolve('permission', name)` is the resolver's own read (registry first, then the metadata service); no `sys_permission_set` row is read; the unit double throws on every `find`, and the dogfood pin deletes the packaged source's rows before it clones. A set whose owning package is disabled resolves to nothing by the reader's rule (`security-catalog.ts:89–90`), so the door answers 404 for it — correct by construction.
6. **New name, mandatory — right.** A target the catalog holds, the source's own name included, is 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Edge, named not faulted: a target name held only by a disabled package resolves to nothing, so the 409 does not fire; the save then meets `refusePackagedBaseOverride`, which `saveMetaItem` asks on every topology ahead of the store write (`protocol.ts:20081`), and the door relays the store's 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. No same-name clone can land.
7. **The copy — right, and it is the ruling's sentence.** `structuredClone(definition)` minus `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS`, then `name` and `label` set. The list is `['_diagnostics', '_draft']` (`METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS`) plus the seven `MetadataProtectionFields` keys (`_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_lockSource`, `_provenance`, `_packageId`, `_packageVersion`, `_lockDocsUrl`) plus `packageId`, `managedBy`, `protection`, `adminScope`, `isDefault`. No facet is enumerated — ADR-0126 §7.1 "whole-definition copy, never param-list assembly" holds, and the deep-equality pin against the source minus the exported list makes a dropped facet red. The two keys the ruling names, `adminScope` and `isDefault`, are on the list; the provenance and package keys execute "no linkage to the base" (§7.1, §9). The response is `{ permissionSet, notice }` with no ancestry field, and the pin asserts the source name is absent from the copy's JSON. The unit test's `it('declares the mutation set and the dropped list once')` pins `_lock` and `_packageId` by name but not `_provenance` or `_packageVersion`; the deep-equality case covers them, so the pin set is complete.
8. **The save — right in behaviour, wrong in its stated mechanism.** `protocol.saveMetaItem({ type: 'permission', name, item, parentVersion: null })`: a `null` parent is `sealedWrite = 'create'` on `main` (`protocol.ts:19910`), the first-write pin, so a row written under the name between the catalog read and the save is refused rather than overwritten; no organization (the ADR-0131 D6 `refuseOrganizationScopedWrite` passes) and no package, so the copy is environment-authored. **Wrong:** the module doc (the comment above the save) and the PR body say the save "asks the one authoring rule every definition-write door asks (`tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal`) … and would be refused, loudly, if a provenance key ever rode across". On `main` that method returns `null` for every type but `flow` (`protocol.ts`, "Scoped to `flow`"); for `permission` a provenance key would be stripped silently by `stripDerivedProvenance`. The guarantee is carried by the dropped-keys list and its pin alone. The behaviour is right; the documented mechanism is not.
9. **The refusal envelope — right.** 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, 401 at the floor, 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` (`validationFailure` and the shape refusal), 404, 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with the code declared for both the unbound and the failed catalog read, 501 when no protocol is composed, and a store refusal relayed with its own status and code through `errorFromThrown`. One divergence from the sibling, named: the catch falls back to 500 where `catalog-activation.ts:272` falls back to 503 for an undeclared throw. Not a contract fault; the seat decides whether the two doors should agree.
10. **The route ledger and the censuses — right.** One new `server-only` row carrying `domain: '/security'`; the activation row's note now says "one of the two"; the ledger census 87 → 88; the dogfood blind-spot census and the matrix docblock move with it (`population`/`reachable`/controls 88, `blindSpot` 0, `keys` 23). No SDK method, for the flow row's reason; the row says a client method reclassifies it to `sdk`. `check-route-envelope` declares `permission-set-clone.ts { handBuilt: 0 }`, which the module's code bears out (every answer is `deps.success` / `deps.error` / `deps.errorFromThrown`). The two `dispatcher-error-vocabulary` rows classify `required` / `invalid_type` as the flow rows do.
11. **The published docs — one page is broken on this head: WRONG, and the FAIL reason.** `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx` (the new section and the pointer) and `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx` (the `permission` row names the door and says the refusal does not name it yet, which agrees with 6110777865 assigning that prose to stage 8) are right. `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` on this head carries the three merge-conflict marker lines (the "ours" line, the equals line, the "theirs" line) at lines 370–374, inside the census table, with two "Files containing at least one elevation read" rows between them (58 and 57). The diff shows them (its lines 142–147), and the file read at `?ref=2bc6c13c…` confirms them. The last commit, `2bc6c13c61` "recount the census after the merge", is where they land. A published docs page would render the markers or fail to build; `Build Docs` on this head is `failure`, and no other PR in this card's history with docs changes has that job red. `check:system-context-census` reads the first matching row by regex (`scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs:1037`), so it may stay green while the page is broken — the gate is not the reader of record here; the build is.
12. **Landing zone — right.** The ruling says "services and rest"; the amendment 6111348289 names the model (`POST /automation/:name/clone`). Both precedents that produce this family — the flow clone and the catalog activation door — live in the runtime dispatcher, and the REST server mounts nothing under this path; the dev's placement follows the measured family. The dev's Q2 (A: server-only, no SDK method) is right for the same reason.
13. **Scope lines — held.** `clone_permission_set` and `ActionParamSchema.carryOver` are untouched (stage 8). No `packages/spec/src` path moves. The dogfood pin deletes a packaged set's `sys_permission_set` rows under a system context inside its own booted temp database; that is measurement setup, not a product deletion, so the card's "deleting existing rows is C7's" line is not crossed.

### ② Semver level

- **What the diff publishes:** one new HTTP route on `@objectstack/runtime` (published, `private: false`, 17.7.0) and the new module `domains/permission-set-clone.ts` with its exports; a ledger row; docs. `packages/qa/dogfood` and `scripts/` are not published; `content/docs` is not a package. No other published package's `src` moves, and no `packages/spec/src` path is touched, so no spec changeset is owed.
- **The changeset:** `.changeset/15204-permission-set-clone-door.md`, `"@objectstack/runtime": minor` — right for an additive route. Its sentences hold against the diff: never reads a `sys_permission_set` row (the double throws, the pin deletes); create-only (`parentVersion: null`); the dropped list as stated; `isSystem` bypasses; anonymous 401; the refusal table; "No existing route changes" (only the activation row's ledger NOTE moved, not its route). `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.
- **Clause-②:** the PR body's second line and the changeset both read `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Right: a path that accepted nothing now accepts `{ name, label }`, and nothing accepted before is refused now.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev OQ1 — the locked-base refusal prose still names the data-door clone (A: leave to stage 8).** Answered: A holds. 6110777865 carries `packaged-base-regime.ts:198` and `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts:343` to stage 8, and the metadata-lifecycle row states the gap in the meantime. Nothing owed here.
2. **Dev OQ2 — route placement in the runtime dispatcher, `server-only`, no client method (A).** Answered: A holds (①.12). Re-open only when an app repository asks for a programmatic clone; the ledger row already says what then changes.
3. **Dev deviation — objectui comments NOT MEASURED, the dispatch's quotes executed verbatim.** Closed by this record: the ruling 6097763840 was read directly, and its Q1 → A sentences ("copies the whole definition under a new name and drops the keys the server declares (`adminScope`, `isDefault`)"; "no linkage to the base"; the flow precedent as the model) are the behaviour measured in ①.5–①.8.
4. **Dev deviation — open PRs not searched.** Covered by the head's two claim guards (`No other open PR may claim the same issue` / `same single-writer path`), both `success`.
5. **Dev deviation — the mid-run merge of `main` and the census recount.** This is where the defect lives. The merge commit `6d4ffaea50` resolved one census conflict by count; the recount commit `2bc6c13c61` left the conflict markers in `system-context.mdx` (①.11). **Escalated as the FAIL reason, with the remedy:** one patch round that removes the three marker lines, keeps exactly one "Files containing at least one elevation read" row (58 if `gen:system-context-census` on the merged tree agrees), runs the docs build (`Build Docs`' own command) and `check:system-context-census` locally, and pushes. The record is re-rendered on that head; nothing in ① or ② outside item 11 and the two text fixes below needs to move.
6. **Not flagged by the dev — escalated to the seat: the door's accept set under a wall is `/meta`'s.** No posture rung is asked, by design (①.4), and `domains/meta.ts` asks none either, so under `group` / `isolated` an organization-scoped `manage_metadata` holder — the leak `activation-gate.ts` records in its header, which is why the §5 gate exists for switches — can create an environment-wide `permission` item through this door exactly as through `PUT /meta/permission/:name` today. ADR-0131 D3's "creation through Setup or the API is refused with a message naming the posture and the capability" is not executed here, and the card's walled-creation refusal pin (triage pointer 6070695107) has no stage. This is not a widening against `/meta` and the ruling's quoted sentences are silent on it, so it is not a FAIL reason of this record; the seat should say whether CD inherits `/meta`'s posture-less accept set (as built, mirroring the flow precedent) or whether the D3 refusal is owed on the catalog doors before 6b-2 lands.
7. **Text fixes owed in the same patch round (no behaviour moves):** the `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` sentence in the module doc above the save and in the PR body (①.8), and the 400 message's "or underscore" (①.2). Optional, the seat's call: align the catch's fallback status with the sibling door (①.9).
8. **Gates pending at render:** `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core (3/6)` were `in_progress` at 19:13Z; their conclusions are read on the next head in any case, since the patch round above moves it.

Implemented-by: `session_01999rKpwstpg8Jysr6vN6JC`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Rerax7QTjKMPCUZxQUtPFR`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

### ① Derived judgments

**The delta (brief item a) — right, and it is the whole change.** `compare/2bc6c13c61...61449d236a`: `ahead_by 1, behind_by 0`, one commit `61449d236a` (parent `2bc6c13c61`), three files: `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` (−4 lines: the ours line, the equals line, the 57 row and the theirs line go; the 58 row between them stays), `packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts` (+9 −5: the 400 message and the comment above the save), `packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.test.ts` (+9 −2: the 400 pin).
